Would a system that disallows debt be better than a system that allows it?
If a society completely forbid debt of any kind would the outcome be a better or worse society than we have in 1st world countries today

It would really suck initially, as most people wouldn't be able to barter to their full benefit. Once established, it would work alright, but would emphasize the benefits of small local farms/shops/mechanics/tradesmen/ect.
You don't think people would be able to globalize under this system?

I won't say it can't happen, but I think it would take longer to fully globalize this plan, due to some regions flourishing and others going bankrupt till they can diversify output. I think it would need a self sustaining local base before it could ever flourish globally. You could also change my mind. My biggest doubts circle around food production/hunting/scavenging, and manufacturing new parts/tools/ammo/equiptment/ect.
How do you keep track of a transfer of value when shipping takes weeks?
A well paid courier will always fit the bill. It's how "riding shotgun" became a thing. If the value is high enough for the product, there will always be suppliers.

It would only be rough at first because we've let the rich get too rich and the poor get too poor. Eventually it would even out and re-prioritize things. But I'm not sure if it would ultimately get better.

Debt is not inherently a bad thing. I think we've just gotten too greedy with interest. Esspecially with things like credit cards. Say I loan you $100 and tack on 30% as repayment. I give you $100 and get $130 back, everyone wins. But with credit cards, it's 30%(ish) ever month. So instead of paying back $130 it can be $100 or $500+. So it's designed to keep you trapped in debt and in all honesty should be illegal practices.

Fair debt is fine. Even something like a mortage or car loan. It helps people progress their lives.

So without debt, instead of keeping the populous drowning in debt, they would just prevent us from saving too much. No matter what, the top will always want the bottom controllably poor and uneducated.

This wouldn't work, because many industries simply can't function without debt.

Farming for instance, relies on credit. This is why there are farmer's credit unions. The idea is that they use their credit to buy new machinery, seeds, livestock, etc. and use their land and expertise to turn a profit, which pays back the loan with small interest. The credit unions are sometimes cooperatively owned, so that the farmers are the ones who earn back the interest through a share scheme.

Fishing also relies on credit, as does mining and manufacturing. There are many industries that go through long cycles of spending before you get revenue. The only way you could avoid this is if you kept a pot of money at all times - the problem is that this "pot" would be a barrier to entry to a bunch of industries. Large multinational corporations have lots of financial freedom because they use their own money rather than credit. So the only people that would benefit from a no-debt economy would be billion dollar corporations. Small businesses would be impossible to start up. People would be living hand to mouth.

The other problem would be housing. Housing development is also an industry that relies upon credit, particularly in startups, because building houses costs money. You have to pay architects, city planners, land owners, construction workers, building material vendors, equipment rental companies, the list goes on. Before you make your first house sale you'll be down several million. Nobody would be able to buy the houses because that requires lending too, so you'd go bankrupt.

The end result would be shanty towns and markets somewhat like the slums of India. These are people who can't get jobs because they can't afford education, and as a result they can't qualify for credit which means they can't buy housing or set up their own businesses. It's an endless cycle.

It wouldn't be great. Debt is not necessarily a bad thing. It enables a company to leverage their position.

Companies also need this to adjust timing of cash flows. As an example a toy company making toys for Christmas needs to borrow many to pay for the cost of manufacturing toys. And when at Christmas sell all the toys will be able to repay the loan with the money made.

With out someone providing a loan only a rich person with existing funds can build the toys company.

Borrowing can enable a poor person to take a risk with the skills they have to build wealth from nothing.

So to answer your question, the result will be the rich get richer and the poor stay poor.
